approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from accepted scored molecules, using high-score quantile parent draws, connected-fragment crossover and local mutation with bounded continuation and saturation handling. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. Stable canonical identities reject duplicates, and a sulfur rule rejects newly introduced outside-envelope signatures relative to the original scored parents. Each fresh surplus pool is ranked by a Gaussian process trained on the entire accepted archive using raw integer Morgan counts and dot-product Tanimoto similarity. It centers and scales the scores, fixes its latent mean, signal variance and observation variance, and selects distinct molecules with correlated Thompson draws. Accepted results update the archive and the best-scoring breeding population.
approach.novelty: Replace the fixed scalar GP assumptions with one joint exact marginal-likelihood fit of constant latent mean, signal variance and observation variance at every existing refit. The count geometry, score normalization and correlated Thompson rule stay fixed. This tests whether accepted labels can set a more useful location and regularization level before new offspring are ranked. Earlier siblings changed fingerprint radius, added information channels, replaced predictive location or removed existing consumers; historical noise ladders fitted only noise, and residual scaling acted after conditioning. The new fitting operation changes the complete posterior coherently and has one joint interpretation. Its success requires delivery to real choices and productive descendants followed by a complete endpoint gain.

observed_bottleneck: The limiting behavior is inconsistent productive progress from fresh offspring, despite useful count-GP guidance. Actual Parent n-1744a1494180 summaries and run logs are complete: mean 0.59645311428869, population SD 0.03397032998399878, seed macros 0.643098123844866/0.563172834083287/0.583088384937917. Its source refits all accepted labels but fixes standardized latent mean to zero, signal variance to one and noise variance to 0.05^2; no accepted-data scalar fitting is performed. The Parent has 648 strict best-parent wins with positive gain mass 17.251535 and sequential incumbent gain 5.819415; weak or concentrated progress remains an observed limitation, while scalar misspecification is an unproven explanation. The stopped radius-menu n-3f67db7b3d96 changed 368/435 feature maps under fixed amplitude/noise, weakened same-label ordering and lost about 0.039992; its radius-regime associations do not diagnose noise or roughness. Earlier binary-feature noise fitting n-9002c3d22369 improved MSE and coverage but lost 0.01596063945276797; the one-sided ladder n-e6bce5cb59ec also lost about 0.017540. Post-hoc residual scaling n-38bcd7569cce improved coverage with unchanged means but lost 0.03814118675118202 on a different, ungated Parent. Descriptor fitting n-5cc22bb8f56b improved ranking yet lost about 0.013060. More recently the joint pairwise-BNN/UCB n-ccb8d255bf00 reached real next fits and descendants but had same-label pair accuracy 0.470128 versus passive GP 0.706399, 801 local wins against weaker parents, only 9.643219 positive gain mass, and 13 completed endpoint losses. Two missing endpoints prevent a complete aggregate; 18 terminal evaluator-only labels never reached learning. Native TabPFN n-5277bf3b7425 and niche breeding n-37a4fc183d94 also weakened absolute progress and complete endpoints. Current location/count-consumer removals n-04741f9b1832, n-161b32768a03 and n-b77e5493be1e support retaining useful count information under their literal conditions, without establishing optimal fixed GP scalars. Thus one source-specified joint fit on unchanged geometry is testable; likelihood, calibration, local wins and chemistry breadth are not substitutes for useful gain.

Its actual queries and primary-source findings remain at the referenced review; no new search query is claimed here. Re-read the pinned official model/driver and paper Appendix F.4. method_change.previous_method: The supplied code Parent n-1744a1494180 fits an exact raw-count Tanimoto GP at fixed standardized mean zero, signal variance one and observation variance 0.05^2, followed by full correlated Thompson pool selection.
method_change.proposed_method: Keep the same raw-count exact GP and sampler but jointly learn the three scalar parameters by bounded deterministic exact marginal likelihood at every existing accepted-archive refit, using the fitted model in all inference blocks.
method_change.rationale: Current evidence favors retaining count information and learned location while leaving their fixed scalar assumptions untested. Iterative Review supplies a concrete exact-GP fitting operation distinct from the failed radius menu, binary noise ladders and post-hoc residual scaling. Scalar misspecification is a testable hypothesis, not a diagnosed cause, and the result belongs to the complete three-scalar fit.

hypothesis: Jointly fit the count-GP constant latent mean, positive signal variance and positive observation variance by exact accepted-archive marginal likelihood, then deliver that single fitted posterior coherently to the unchanged correlated Thompson selector.

finding_summary.headline: Joint GP fitting changed search, but better prediction error did not deliver useful gains
finding_summary.insights: The experiment rules out lack of delivery as the explanation for this recipe’s failure: fitted models changed accepted molecules, later training and actual breeding. It also narrows the predictive bottleneck. Smaller same-label squared error and wider noise-inclusive intervals were insufficient for useful discovery; ordering did not improve consistently, and extra local wins came against weaker parents with smaller gains. The exact joint likelihood-fitting operation borrowed from the literature worked computationally, but its transfer to tiny, repeatedly fitted adaptive archives on the retained raw-count geometry did not improve endpoints. This does not test the source’s larger random-subset regression setting or identify a separate contribution from mean, signal or noise. Successful optimization also needs a limited reading: 97 fits stopped on function tolerance above the gradient tolerance, 11 reached the signal floor and 167 the noise floor. Seven early near-constant archives produced almost collapsed latent intervals covering none of their next 70 labels, even though noise-inclusive intervals covered 61; observation uncertainty is a different quantity from the latent uncertainty passed to selection. These are measured boundaries, not evidence for an automatic bounds or optimizer rescue. The molecular assessment likewise finds slightly more new cores without stronger typed-core descendant gains or independent leading families, alongside persistent stereochemical and local-geometry problems; fewer reactive attachments do not establish feasible chemistry or explain the score causally. The registered complete exposed miss ends this fixed joint-fit recipe. A future revision would require new evidence and planning; scalar attribution, mediation, broader molecular feasibility and the campaign’s reliable-gain goal remain open.
finding_summary.results: All 435 joint fits moved the model and its predictive distribution, and 2,216 of 4,350 accepted choices strictly differed from the original GP under the same selection mask and random draw. Of these changed choices, 2,150 reached the next fit; 638 later produced 2,228 distinct accepted direct children. This was a fully exposed intervention, with all 15 sessions completing. On the same selected labels, MSE improved from 0.00810 to 0.00735 in aggregate and improved in every task/seed session. Ordering remained mixed: pair accuracy rose slightly from 0.67051 to 0.67247, while mean batch Spearman fell from 0.44131 to 0.44005; all three sitagliptin sessions worsened on both ranking measures. The fitted observation variance raised diagnostic noise-inclusive coverage from 76.60% to 89.95%, but latent coverage used to characterize allocation fell from 76.46% to 75.22%. More offspring beat their generating parents (763 versus 648), yet those parents and offspring had lower absolute scores. Positive gain mass fell from 17.2515 to 15.1509 and sequential incumbent gain from 5.8194 to 5.1026. Mean final score fell from 0.59645 to 0.54867, a matched difference of −0.04779 against the required +0.002. There were 4 endpoint wins and 11 losses; seed macro differences were −0.15366, +0.01987 and −0.00957, and population standard deviation rose from 0.03397 to 0.04206. The primary result includes the Parent’s late deco_hop breakthrough.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich, seed-specific heterocycles retain reactive attachments, difficult unsaturation and unspecified stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: Node n-0142fbe4db04 produces fused azaaromatic amides and ketones, linked nitrogen-rich heterocycles, aryl aliphatic amines, carbonyl-rich nitrogen rings, and fluorinated nonaromatic imino/lactam systems. Ring construction and heteroatom introduction are abundant. The complete Child accepted output has median 28 heavy atoms and a 1-118 range; median perceived ring count is 4, with 0-15 across optimizer observations. The digest's ring-closure-string incidences are 0.9805-1.0 and aromatic-string incidences 0.5529-1.0 across the five objectives. These are molecule-level text incidences, not ring counts or fractions of aromatic atoms. The lower aromatic incidence belongs to a family whose two strongest seed leaders have no perceived aromatic rings. Neutral strings do not imply absent basic amines. All assigned tetrahedral and double-bond stereochemistry counts are zero; RDKit perceives unassigned tetrahedral centres in 2784/4350 Child versus 2455/4350 Parent optimizer observations, and unspecified potentially stereogenic double bonds in 1049/4350 versus 1192/4350. This is incomplete specification, not proof that every flagged centre is configurationally stable or every molecule needs stereochemistry. Canonical isomeric identities remain the acceptance/ancestry keys; nonisomeric Murcko cores are separate descriptive groupings. All 15 Child and 15 authoritative published Parent n-1744a1494180 trajectories and their accepted-lineage logs were read: each side has 4500 accepted observations, including 4350 optimizer observations and 150 repeated session-initial observations. Each objective has 900 observations, including 870 optimizer observations. No supplied path or objective is missing, and context.comparison separately reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, with all three Search seeds and no profile mismatch. All 290 optimizer observations per session match emitted and observed original-parent receipts. Final Child retained identities match the final retained64 receipts exactly; Parent retained64 is reconstructed from its score/serial greedy rule and agrees with recorded final best/mean. No terminal evaluator-only observations are inferred here. In the per-task text C(seed,task):line means /projects/standard/adeshwal/shared/zhou2577/SPIRAL/.worktrees/slot-0/runs/staging/seed-{seed}/trajectories/{task}.jsonl, and P(seed,task):line means /projects/standard/adeshwal/shared/zhou2577/SPIRAL/runs/SPIRAL2/nodes/n-1744a1494180/seed-{seed}/trajectories/{task}.jsonl. Line equals evaluation in these files. Exact citations and log line identities are in .slots/L01-resume-20261004/r36-slot0-molecular/citation_ledger.json and trajectory_audit.json; supplementary retention checks and all read-source hashes accompany them. All cited_smiles entries use the trusted Child trajectories. The output changes liabilities rather than uniformly resolving them: Child/Parent molecule incidences are N-halogen 438/786, O-halogen 92/217, S-halogen 16/93 and peroxide 95/127, each out of 4350 optimizer observations; classes overlap. Sulfur remains in 830/4350 versus 1100/4350. No sulfur-envelope activation claim is made by these counts. Cyclic carbon bearing at least two double bonds occurs in 122/4350 versus 6/4350; 113 Child observations belong to one nonaromatic/carbonyl family. Ring alkynes occur in 2 versus 13 observations. These are topology flags requiring chemical interpretation, not measured stability, toxicity, strain or synthesis. The output includes recognizable medicinal-chemistry motifs but insufficient consistently conventional local bonding, geometry and stereochemical specification to call overall synthetic plausibility more than questionable. Across the matched accepted records, strict wins over original best generating parents are 763/4350 Child versus 648/4350 Parent, while summed positive margins are 15.150850854195372 versus 17.25153528627184. Mean optimizer label is 0.3385592697330084 versus 0.372049560842182 and mean best-generating-parent label 0.4083437688500384 versus 0.4553040448335957; additional wins therefore coexist with weaker parent baselines. Sequential incumbent gain sums are 5.1026183058503305 versus 5.819415048695714, and batch-frozen sums 6.786994332753656 versus 9.341378012076637. Those last two quantities have different meanings: batch-frozen sums can credit multiple same-batch molecules for overlapping gains. These descriptive sums pool unlike score landscapes and do not replace the supplied endpoints. Typed nonisomeric Murcko first arrivals, absent from all preceding accepted records including initials, total 1832 Child versus 1820 Parent across sessions; generic-core first arrivals total 1172 versus 1117. Empty-core optimizer observations are separately 37 versus 111. Among typed first arrivals, 310/1832 versus 262/1820 beat their original best parent, but only 103 versus 107 establish a new sequential incumbent. Of those typed first arrivals, 518/1832 versus 485/1820 later have accepted direct children; the session-deduplicated child unions contain 1771 versus 1791 observations with positive-gain sums 5.957069101687759 versus 6.035552260703594. Generic first arrivals have 210/1172 versus 163/1117 parent wins, 68 versus 71 incumbent wins, and 331/1172 versus 299/1117 parents with accepted direct children. These are session-summed core events and direct-child unions, not independent global scaffolds or all recursive descendants; a losing first arrival does not imply every later same-core molecule descends from it. Full seed/task figures are retained in the audit. All top-ten sets share at least one founder across all ten leaders. Child sets contain one to three distinct initial founders, with five of fifteen sets containing only one, versus four of fifteen Parent sets. Per-set founder/leader-incidence HHI is 1/3-1 for both; this denominator differs from the ten-leader coverage denominator. Final retained64 sets preserve the same concentration, with exact per-founder incidences, direct-parent counts and ancestry depths reported in the audit. Both crossover parents and deduplication per leader are retained; these are recorded ancestry associations, not independent founder contributions. Supplied mean endpoints are Child 0.5486666647656643 and Parent 0.59645311428869; supplied seed macro differences are -0.15365823573892295, +0.019873659150646983 and -0.009574771980801033. Chemistry, extra core arrivals or local wins cannot stand in for that mixed seed evidence. No model-activation or individual-parameter causal conclusion belongs to this report.

per_task.generated_character: Optimizer molecules span 2-47 heavy atoms, with median 25 and median three perceived rings, versus Parent median 24 heavy atoms. The seed-0 leader is a 23-heavy-atom, five-ring methylamino/N-methyl aromatic ketone with a pyridyl end and a fused methylene ether; seed 1 gives a 25-heavy-atom, four-ring fused azaaromatic carboxamide bearing pyridyl hydroxymethyl and methylthio substituents; seed 2 gives a 25-heavy-atom pyrrole-fused seven-membered diene, hydroxyl/fluoromethyl substitution and an N-chloro pyridyl amide. Thus ordinary amide/thioether chemistry coexists with unusual fusion patterns and reactive N substitution. The compact seed-1 leader has the most recognizable local functional groups, but its fused topology still lacks a synthesis or conformer assessment. C(0,zaleplon_mpo):245, C(1,zaleplon_mpo):255 and C(2,zaleplon_mpo):234 are the seed leaders.
liabilities: Direct N-halogen bonds occur in 166/870 optimizer observations and 10/30 molecules in the pooled per-seed top tens. N-hydroxy amides and methylthio groups are chemically different and should not be blanket-classified with N-halogen bonds.

The seven-membered cyclic cumulene at C(2,zaleplon_mpo):265 scores 0.4086104282862019. It is a geometry concern rather than proof that ordinary medium rings are impossible; no 3D feasibility measurement was made.
missing_features: Reliable conventional alternatives to reactive amide-N halogen substitution are incompletely represented within the seed-2 leading series. The stronger seed-1 molecule already lacks N/O-halogen bonds, so such bonds are not a universal requirement.
Independent plausible aromatic/carbonyl organizations remain limited among leaders despite many new ring cores. The visible labels identify no exact absent target pharmacophore.
The substituted medium-ring series lacks specified stereochemical identity and verified ring geometry; the absence of stereotags is not evidence that the whole output is achiral.

per_task.generated_character: This output is larger: median 36 heavy atoms versus Parent 31, range 2-118, and median five perceived rings. Seed 0 produces a 29-heavy-atom linked azaaryl fused dione with N-ethynyl and aminomethyl substituents; seed 1 a 32-heavy-atom linked azaaryl carbonyl/oxygen heterocycle with carbon-linked nitrile, ethynyl and methoxy groups. Two of 870 proposals contain ring alkynes, and the seed-2 leader carries an unspecified alkenyl geometry and a large linked nitrogen ring. N-ethynyl dione substitution in seed 0 also needs environment-specific reactivity assessment.
missing_features: The Child does not demonstrate a comparably strong alternative to the Parent's late high-label fused arrangement. Its different chemistry is not evidence that the Parent's reactive attachments should be introduced.

A reliable route to compact, chemically credible alternative connectivities is incomplete: aromatic concatenation adds substantial mass without matching the compact leaders, while a larger leading nitrogen ring has no demonstrated accessible geometry.
The observed scores do not identify a specific absent motif or distinguish the necessity of many tied peripheral substitutions.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
